messages:
Priya S.: Received an escalated ticket from a customer — their A/B rollout dashboard shows Variant labels flipped. They say counts and allocations look reversed even though traffic and logs show the correct variant served. :frowning:

Chandra R.: Thanks, linking their console screenshot and example request IDs?

Priya S.: Screenshot here: https://redwood.internal/snap/abc123 (customer masked). Example req ids: r_20240301_93a, r_20240301_9b2. They reported this started after the analytics deployment yesterday night.

Eli K.: I can repro in the UI quickly — open an experiment, switch cohort granularity to hourly and variant A shows B's counts and vice versa. Totals still equal the sum of variants (so nothing lost), labels appear swapped.

Chandra R.: If totals are unchanged, sounds like a mapping issue between variant_key and variant_label at render time. Could be the join on variants table returned rows in a different order after the new db index. Will check the query used by the dashboard.

Marta L.: Alert-bot also fired for sudden label drift on that experiment: :eyes: @Chandra we saw an anomaly exactly at 2024-03-01T03:12Z when the analytics job was redeployed.

Chandra R.: Found the dashboard query. The frontend does:

```sql
SELECT v.label, a.count FROM assignments a
JOIN variants v ON a.variant_id = v.id
WHERE a.experiment_id = :exp
ORDER BY v.sort_index
```

But our migration last night removed the sort_index column population for newly cached variants — many rows have NULL and the DB returns unspecified order, which matches the swapped appearance.

Eli K.: So backend counts are correct, frontend ordering is unstable when sort_index NULL. We should not rely on DB ordering. Quick fix in UI to sort by v.label or variant_id would stabilize.

Priya S.: Customer is quite upset because the dashboard is used for decision ops. They asked for ETA on a fix and whether the raw API/CSV is accurate.

Chandra R.: Raw API (assignments endpoint) returns correct mapping because it uses variant_id as the key. Confirmed via logs for the two req ids — they show correct variant assignment. So we can tell customer their telemetry is intact.

Eli K.: I'll push a UI hotfix to explicitly ORDER BY COALESCE(v.sort_index, v.id) and fall back to label as tie-breaker. Minimal change, no migrations.

Marta L.: Can we also backfill the missing sort_index for new variants so future queries aren't unstable? I can run a small job to set sort_index = id for rows where NULL.

Chandra R.: Yes, plan: (1) UI hotfix rollout (canary 5% now), (2) backfill job to set missing sort_index, (3) add a lint check in the migrations to ensure sort_index is populated.

Eli K.: Deploying hotfix now. @deploy-bot starting canary.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for branch fix/variant-order-20240301 — route 5% to canary.

Priya S.: I'll update the customer: explain that ingestion/counts are correct, UI ordering bug introduced by missing sort_index, hotfix rolling out, backfill and migration lint planned. ETA: hotfix live in ~10m, backfill within 2 hours, migration lint in next deploy.

Chandra R.: Backfill script ready, will run after hotfix verification. SQL:

```sql
UPDATE variants
SET sort_index = id
WHERE sort_index IS NULL;
```

Running as a low-priority batch to avoid locking.

Eli K.: Canary looks good at 5% — variant labels stable for the sample experiment. Increasing to 50%.

deploy-bot: Canary scaled to 50%.

Priya S.: Customer replied: "Thanks — much better, will monitor. Please keep us posted." :relieved:

Marta L.: Backfill completed, no locking issues. Will monitor metrics.

Chandra R.: Added a migration test to CI to ensure sort_index can't be NULL after variant creation. Also added an instrumentation event to alert when dashboard join returns non-deterministic ordering (detected via missing sort keys).

Priya S.: Closing the loop with the customer and creating a short postmortem doc. Will attach links to the hotfix PR and backfill job in the ticket.

Eli K.: Postmortem checklist: root cause, quick mitigation (UI ORDER BY), permanent fix (backfill + migration lint), and customer communication.

Priya S.: Thanks everyone. Marking as resolved.
